slot.brief: Provide a P–V diagram of a cycle composed of an isobaric expansion, an isothermal, and a constant-volume leg; ask for the net work done over the full cycle and heat exchanged in one leg using the first law with monatomic Cv.

stem: For the cycle shown, the gas is monatomic and ideal. What are the net work done by the gas over the full cycle and the heat absorbed during $A\to B$?

verdicts.working: On A→B, W = PΔV = 100 J and ΔU = (3/2)Δ(PV) = 150 J, so Q_AB = 250 J. On B→C, W = (PV)ln(V_C/V_B) = −200 ln 2 J; C→A has zero work. Thus W_cycle = 100 − 200 ln 2 J.

working:
$W_{AB}=100(2-1)=100\ \text{J}$; $W_{BC}=P_BV_B\ln(V_C/V_B)=200\ln(1/2)=-200\ln2\ \text{J}$; $W_{CA}=0$, so $W_{\rm cycle}=100-200\ln2\ \text{J}$. $\Delta U_{AB}=\frac32\Delta(PV)=\frac32(200-100)=150\ \text{J}$; $Q_{AB}=\Delta U_{AB}+W_{AB}=250\ \text{J}$.

Independent check: On A→B, W = PΔV = 100 J and ΔU = (3/2)Δ(PV) = 150 J, so Q_AB = 250 J. On B→C, W = (PV)ln(V_C/V_B) = −200 ln 2 J; C→A has zero work. Thus W_cycle = 100 − 200 ln 2 J.
solution:
For a complete cycle, $W_{\rm cycle}=W_{AB}+W_{BC}+W_{CA}$, with $W_{AB}=100(2-1)=100\,\text{J}$, $W_{BC}=200\ln(1/2)=-200\ln2\,\text{J}$, and $W_{CA}=0$.
$$W_{\rm cycle}=100-200\ln2\,\text{J}$$
For a monatomic ideal gas, $\Delta U_{AB}=\frac32\Delta(PV)=150\,\text{J}$, so $Q_{AB}=\Delta U_{AB}+W_{AB}=250\,\text{J}$. Thus the result is $(100-200\ln2,\ 250)\,\text{J}$.

figure.description: Draw a P–V graph with volume V (L) on the horizontal axis and pressure P (kPa) on the vertical axis. Mark A at (1, 100), B at (2, 100), and C at (1, 200). Join A to B with a horizontal line and an arrow A→B; join B to C with a downward-curving isotherm and an arrow B→C; join C to A with a vertical line and an arrow C→A. Label AB “isobaric”, BC “isothermal”, and CA “constant volume”.

draft.distractor_notes: B: reports the internal-energy change alone as heat. C: uses the wrong sign for work during isothermal compression. D: uses the initial-cycle value of $PV$ instead of $P_BV_B$ for the isothermal leg.
